full_judgment: "Mr. Abul Quasem, learned Advocate-on-record, appearing for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division has committed error in law by setting aside the concurrent judgments and decrees of the Court below i.e. Trial and Appellate Court without discussing and assessing the evidence on record decreed the suit and as such, the judgment decreeing the suit has been perverse and invalid being hit by Rule 31 of Order 41 of the Code of Civil Procedure which can not be sustained in law; that on proper discussion and assessment of the evidence, the trial Court having arrived at its decision that the plaintiff had utterly failed to prove his title and possession in the suit land and he having dismissed the suit which being upheld by the learned Judges of the Appellate Court whereby finding of fact was concluded, the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division by comparing signatures of Harala Das, the alleged executor of the so called mortgage deed, attesting witnesses Chitta Ranjan Das and Golap Ali Mollah appearing therein under Section 73 of the Evidence Act, with admitted signatures of exhibited registered deeds arrived at a finding that the said mortgage deed Exhivit-1 as false and forged, thus has committed error in law by ignoring and not appreciating this vital aspect in his judgment of reversal.
